cases.threat: development key promoted to production identity
cases.invariant: production trust roots are distinct from sico.sapp.signature.v0 development keys

cases.threat: single online key compromise authorizes every release
cases.invariant: root, release, recovery, rotation and revocation roles are separated with explicit thresholds

cases.threat: identity-provider or CI claim is accepted without policy binding
cases.invariant: issuer, subject, workflow and repository claims are matched against a signed publisher policy

cases.threat: compromised or expired signer silently remains authoritative
cases.invariant: rotation and revocation are signed, versioned, time-bounded and recoverable from an offline root

cases.threat: first-upload squatting captures a public app id
cases.invariant: namespace ownership is an explicit signed registry grant rather than an inference from package app.id

cases.threat: Unicode or case variants impersonate an existing namespace
cases.invariant: public names use canonical lowercase ASCII labels and are compared byte-for-byte

cases.threat: namespace transfer changes publisher without consumer visibility
cases.invariant: transfer is a separately signed event retaining old and new owner identities plus an audit reference

cases.threat: deleted namespace is immediately reused for unrelated code
cases.invariant: tombstones and reuse policy are monotonic and included in discovery evidence

cases.threat: registry serves bytes different from advertised content
cases.invariant: clients fetch by digest, verify byte length and digest, then repeat local strict package verification

cases.threat: mutable tag or channel is treated as immutable identity
cases.invariant: names and channels resolve only to signed immutable release records and package digests

cases.threat: mirror or CDN injects authority through transport metadata
cases.invariant: transport, cache headers and mirrors are never trust roots

cases.threat: split-view registry hides or forks publication history
cases.invariant: signed checkpoints and inclusion evidence are independently cacheable and auditable

cases.threat: older signed metadata is replayed
cases.invariant: trusted root, snapshot and release sequence numbers never decrease

cases.threat: stale but valid metadata freezes a client
cases.invariant: online metadata expires and clients retain last trusted version and expiry state

cases.threat: metadata from different repository states is mixed
cases.invariant: one signed snapshot binds the exact release records and package digests used in a transaction

cases.threat: partial download replaces a working revision
cases.invariant: download, verify and install occur in staging and activation is atomic after every trust gate passes

cases.threat: mutable version ranges produce different builds
cases.invariant: published releases bind an immutable canonical dependency lock graph

cases.threat: dependency confusion selects an unintended registry or namespace
cases.invariant: each dependency identity includes registry, namespace, package name, version and digest

cases.threat: transitive package gains undeclared host authority
cases.invariant: effective capabilities are the verified closure of root and locked dependencies and still intersect host grants

cases.threat: yanked or revoked dependency silently changes an existing lock
cases.invariant: yank affects new resolution while revocation is an explicit signed security decision evaluated by policy

cases.threat: security report channel leaks credentials or user data
cases.invariant: public metadata contains no secrets and disclosure intake defines redaction and retention rules

cases.threat: attacker suppresses a security advisory
cases.invariant: advisories are signed append-only records addressable independently of mutable release pages

cases.threat: advisory ambiguously identifies affected artifacts
cases.invariant: affected ranges are accompanied by exact release and package digests where known

cases.threat: untrusted registry text is rendered as active content
cases.invariant: descriptions and advisories are bounded inert text with no script, markup execution or shell interpolation

cases.threat: automatic rollback installs a compromised older release
cases.invariant: rollback requires an explicit signed recovery authorization or local user recovery policy

cases.threat: rollback crosses publisher identity or app id
cases.invariant: recovery remains within the immutable production app identity unless a separately authorized migration exists

cases.threat: failed update destroys the last known-good revision
cases.invariant: hosts retain a verified prior revision until new activation and recovery checks complete

cases.threat: rollback restores obsolete permission grants
cases.invariant: capability fingerprint drift always causes re-evaluation even for previously installed revisions

cases.threat: one version string is used for language, package and API compatibility
cases.invariant: every compatibility surface has an independent explicit identifier

cases.threat: unknown schema fields are guessed or ignored
cases.invariant: security-relevant canonical records reject unknown schema versions, fields and enum values

cases.threat: app version ordering accepts non-SemVer ambiguous strings
cases.invariant: published app releases use canonical SemVer 2.0.0 without leading zeroes and compare precedence by the specification

cases.threat: client installs a release requiring unsupported runtime or WIT contracts
cases.invariant: release records declare exact minimum and supported compatibility identifiers before package download or execution
